original_question: How can one characterize the optical symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines, namely the local symplectic transformations realizable by finite collections of mirrors, inside the full space of symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the unnumbered problem in the Serge Tabachnikov section, subsection "Optical transformations of the space of oriented lines," which asks for a characterization of the local symplectic transformations of the space of oriented lines that are realizable by a finite collection of mirrors, viewed inside the full class of local symplectic transformations of that space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact object and task almost verbatim: the space of oriented lines, the local symplectic transformations coming from finite collections of mirrors, and the goal of characterizing those optical maps inside all symplectic transformations of the oriented-line space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: the paper is discussing the space of oriented lines in Euclidean n-space, interpreted as rays of light. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The symplectic structure is not arbitrary; it is the one induced from the canonical symplectic structure on the cotangent bundle of the ambient n-dimensional space by symplectic reduction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The realizable maps are local optical/billiard reflection maps coming from finitely many smooth mirrors, where a mirror is a smooth hypersurface locally given as the graph of a function of n-1 variables. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The nearby context motivates the problem by a function-counting heuristic: the oriented-line space has much larger local symplectic freedom than the data of a mirror, so the mirror-realizable class is expected to be a very small subset of all local symplectic transformations. Making that asymmetry explicit helps the question stand alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

There are no extra algebraic hypotheses here—no ring/field choice, homogeneity or degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic quantifier of the form "for all sufficiently large m"—so the hidden assumptions to spell out are geometric, smoothness, and locality assumptions instead. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
refined_question: In Euclidean n-space, let L be the space of oriented lines, equipped with the symplectic structure induced from the canonical symplectic structure on the cotangent bundle of the ambient space by symplectic reduction. A smooth mirror, i.e. a smooth hypersurface locally given as the graph of a function of n-1 variables, defines a local optical reflection map on L; hence any finite collection of smooth mirrors defines, locally, a composition of such symplectic reflection maps. How can one characterize, within the full set of local symplectic transformations of L, the subclass consisting exactly of those local symplectic transformations realizable by reflection in finitely many smooth mirrors? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
justification: This rewrite stays as close as possible to the paper because the paper does not state a broader conjecture here; it gives only this unnumbered problem under Serge Tabachnikov's subsection "Optical transformations of the space of oriented lines." The draft was already essentially correct, so the only additions are the ambient Euclidean n-space, the origin of the symplectic structure via symplectic reduction from the cotangent bundle, and the fact that "finite collections of mirrors" means local compositions of reflections in smooth hypersurfaces. I did not broaden the question beyond mirror-realizable local symplectic maps, and I did not add any alternate formulation because none is stated as equivalent in the nearby text. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
